Sam — thanks for the doc and the clear priorities. I've routed sections 3/5/7 to our security team; David and Stephanie pulled answers together below (summary) and we'll complete the questionnaire PDF by EOD Friday. Short answers here to accelerate procurement scheduling: 

Section 3 — Data classification & handling:
- PII handling: Redwood does not require customers to send unnecessary PII. For fields that are collected, we support field-level redaction and customer-configurable masking rules at ingestion time. Our hosted offering can be configured to redact or hash sensitive fields before they are persisted.
- Data retention: Customers can set retention policies per workspace; default retention for logs is 30 days, configurable up to 7 years for long-term audit data with enterprise add-on. Stored model inputs/outputs are retained per customer-configured policy; we support automatic purges and exports.
- Data in transit & at rest: All customer data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we use AES-256 with customer-managed keys available via KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Section 5 — Logging & audit:
- Audit logs: We provide immutable audit trails for admin actions, API keys creation/rotation, and support access events. Logs include actor, timestamp, action, and request identifiers.
- Access logging: Request-level logs can be configured to exclude full PII fields; you can enable structured logging to capture metadata without payloads.
- Log retention & export: Logs can be exported to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or to customer S3 buckets for long-term retention and e-discovery.

Section 7 — Support / administrative access (break-glass):
- Break-glass workflow: Redwood requires a documented request with justification, approval by an assigned FinTrust approver, and time-bound access tokens for the session. Each session is recorded and instrumented; all actions are captured in audit logs.
- Least privilege: Support and ops roles are scoped with least-privilege by default. Engineers do not have default read access to unredacted data. Access is elevated only via the break-glass process and is temporary.
- Session capture: Interactive sessions (if applicable) are session-recorded and the transcripts/artifacts are stored alongside the audit log entry.

Next steps: 
- We will fill the attached questionnaire and send the completed PDF by EOD Friday (2026-08-28).
- Proposed technical deep-dive with David on Wed Sep 2, 9:30am PT (I will send an invite).

Let us know if you want us to include our SOC 2 artifact checklist or a sample audit log extract for review.

Best,
Marissa
